slot.brief: State the geometry and hybridisation of XeF4 (square planar) among options; simple structure identification.

stem: What are the geometry and hybridisation of the central atom in $\text{XeF}_4$?

verdicts.working: Xe has 4 Xe–F bonds and 2 lone pairs: 6 electron domains give an octahedral arrangement. The two lone pairs are opposite, leaving a square-planar molecular geometry; the conventional hybridisation is sp³d².

working:
$\text{XeF}_4$: 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs around Xe.\
Six electron domains give $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation; the two lone pairs occupy opposite positions.\
Molecular geometry: square planar.

Independent check: Xe has 4 Xe–F bonds and 2 lone pairs: 6 electron domains give an octahedral arrangement. The two lone pairs are opposite, leaving a square-planar molecular geometry; the conventional hybridisation is sp³d².
solution:
Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, so there are 6 electron domains around the central atom.
$$\text{Hybridisation}=sp^3d^2$$
The two lone pairs occupy opposite positions in an octahedral arrangement, leaving a square-planar molecular geometry.
